answer: Identity registration in an agent economy costs a non-refundable stake plus a signed compute attestation at a fixed throughput, so flooding a poll means paying that stake and burning real cycles for every fake identity. Each relay caps how many fresh agents one operator can seat per checkpoint, and a vine of downstream referrals inherits the parent's risk score, so a farm collapses when one leaf is slashed. Marginal cost stays linear while influence stays flat: a wharf of clones gets its bond frozen, an echo of verified work is what unlocks it.
